document.title: Discussions w/CENTCOM re: Sy Hersh Article
document.authors: Office of the Secretary of Defense (Rumsfeld)
document.publisher: National Security Archive (GWU), New Documents Detail America's Strategic Response to 9/11
document.note: [Secret] Rumsfeld is concerned by Hersh's report that CENTCOM failed to fire on a convoy thought to carry Mullah Omar. He had told Franks to hit it if anyone wiggled, and says he has a high tolerance for possible error in strikes.

events.description: Rumsfeld, in Taos, questioned Franks about the targeting process for Predator-located targets and then set out guidance about high tolerance for error.
Rumsfeld memo recording discussions with CENTCOM about Sy Hersh's New Yorker article claiming the CENTCOM lawyer delayed a strike.
Franks called Rumsfeld about a possible target; Rumsfeld gave immediate authority to hit it and obtained President's agreement within 4½ minutes.
Rumsfeld, in Taos, questioned Franks about the targeting process (Predator, Hellfire, CAP aircraft, collateral damage decision) and later asked about 15 timing questions.
Franks called Rumsfeld about a possible target. Rumsfeld gave authority to hit it if anyone wiggled and obtained the President's agreement within 4½ minutes.
Rumsfeld memo on discussions with CENTCOM about the Sy Hersh New Yorker article, saying a CENTCOM lawyer allegedly delayed a strike. Franks denied it and Rumsfeld doubted he got the full story.

Rumsfeld told Franks that getting bin Laden, Omar and senior Taliban and al-Qaeda leaders is vital, that he tolerates a high risk of error, and that Franks should lean far forward and always be able to reach him or Wolfowitz.

sources_cited: Sy Hersh article in The New Yorker
key_claims: Rumsfeld gave Franks standing authority to strike targets immediately if they were at risk of escaping, pending presidential approval.
Franks denied that the CENTCOM lawyer slowed the strike, though Rumsfeld suspected he had not been given the full story.
Rumsfeld instructed Franks to have a high tolerance for error and strike valid targets without waiting if neither he nor Wolfowitz could be reached.
Bin Laden, Mullah Omar and senior Taliban and al-Qaeda leaders were the top-priority targets in October 2001.
